_what: R10 AS ROWS. One row per OBJECT IN THE FRAME: what it is, whether anything outside this lane says it should be there, whether it could be built and used, and the verdict. Consumed by pipeline/scripts/existence_check.py, which is spawned by build_room after every render and BLOCKS the build.
_law: The object list is DERIVED FROM THE BUILT SCENE (sheet_recon.assemblies_from_dump), never kept here — R9b: a rule that names the objects it applies to will always exempt the next one.

IDENTITY IS SIGNED, CONSEQUENCES ARE MEASURED. No program can look at a box and know it is a drawer, so the row declares; the checker then holds the declaration to the scene — a named support must exist and touch, a claimed reveal must measure, a 'remove' must actually be gone.
`pending` is refused BY NAME. So are `tbd`, `todo` and `later`.
The unrowed backlog RATCHETS and may only fall. A machine that hard-fails every historical instance on day one gets switched off and joins them (R13).
_why_it_exists: R8 governs HOW an object is made and R9 governs WHERE it goes. R10 was written 2026-08-05 because nothing governed WHETHER IT SHOULD EXIST, and on 2026-08-17 two independent critics filed three defects of exactly that class against p2r47 — a foot bench with no load path, drawer fronts with no way to open them, and a room with no skirting, sockets or switches. The round's own triage accepted all three with the same sentence: no instrument in this repo can see it.

required_elements.why_required: A plastered wall meeting a wood floor is not finished without a skirting or a recessed shadow gap; the junction is drawn on every interior elevation. C2 p2r47 item 10: 'no skirting or shadow-gap where wall meets floor on ANY wall'. Height and projection are DR-sourced for the 2700-3200 mm ceiling band (knowledge/_inbox/nlm-th-bedroom-services).

The sconces over the bed are LIT, so something must switch them from somewhere reachable, and a bedroom has sockets. C2 p2r47 item 10: 'no switch plate anywhere, including beside the bed for the sconces; no sockets'. Heights are DR-sourced (door switch 1200-1250 AFFL, bedside switch 600-700, concealed bedside socket 300-350).

objects.identity: Recessed downlight trim ring, 96 mm, sitting in the ceiling plane.
objects.exists: not-in-drawing: element 5 RCP
objects.why: RESOLVED p2r49/p2r50, and the R10 rung is what found it. Filed unresolved when this ledger opened: the trim sat at z 2734-2740 under a 2800 soffit, so every recessed can in the room hung 60 mm below the ceiling it is recessed into, on every frame this lane has shipped. THE CAUSE was one parameter carrying two things — `_recessed_trim` was handed the FIXTURE's z, and the fixture sits at `ceiling - 60` because an emitter coplanar with the geometry it lights self-shadows. That stand-off is right for the light and wrong for the trim. The light keeps it; the geometry now takes the ceiling. Measured after the fix: trim 2794.0-2799.5 under a 2800.0 soffit (a 5.5 mm flange, flush), aperture 2790.0-2793.0 recessed 7-10 mm above it.

objects.why: C2 p2r47 item 10, and its grounding is the sharpest R10 sentence either critic wrote: the sconces over the bed are LIT, so they must be switched from somewhere reachable. Every position is derived from the opening or the nightstand it serves, so moving the door moves the switch. The carrier is named as the CLASS 'wall' and not as one mass because the three plates sit on three DIFFERENT walls — the door switch on the east wall, the two bedside plates on the BF14 slat wall standing in front of it. The checker refused the first draft of this row, which named wall_4: the plate is nowhere near it. NOTE p2r49: filed as FIX on the day it was built — the blind critic caught the mounting detail in the first frame it appeared in, which is the ladder working rather than a defect surviving.
objects.fix_by: Give each faceplate a flat MOUNTING BLOCK behind it. C2 filed it against the very object this round added (p2r49 item 16: "the switch plate floats on the slat wall with no mounting block, recess or shadow") and it is right as construction: the plate spans x5193-5203, i.e. it lands flush with the slat faces and bridges the gaps between them, and you cannot screw a faceplate to a slat. A real installation cuts the slats back to a flat plaster or ply pad. The pad is a box with radii, so R8 sends it to the builder.

objects.identity: RESOLVED 2026-08-24 - not a wire and not a separate object: the vertical SHADOW REVEAL between the millwork tall unit's end panel and the painted wall, at the frame's extreme left. Named from p2r54's OWN MATMASK (the probe that filed this row used the idmask, whose roster was bed-focused and returned id 0): 84 of the line's 106 pixels carry material id 39 = m_millwork_oak_veneer_photo, the remainder antialiasing between palette levels, with ceiling_paint (id 14) in the adjacent column x=21. objects.exists: not-in-drawing: a shadow gap is a millwork DETAIL rather than a mass, so no sheet rect can correspond to it; it is there because the tall unit's end panel stops short of the wall, which is the reveal the millwork is built with
objects.why: R10 question 1 is answered and the answer changes the verdict: nothing here is an unexplained mass. C2 (p2r54, blind-local) was RIGHT about the pixels - a thin dark line descending from the top edge - and wrong only about what makes them, which is what a blind critic is for. What failed was the BUILDER's probe. Two errors, both measurable today: (1) its recorded coordinates do not hold the feature. It wrote 'a black angular mass ~40 px at x 30-45, y 150-230 of 2400x1800'; that window in p2r54 measures min luma 0.6549, mean 0.6799, and contains ZERO pixels below 0.10. The real feature is a ONE-PIXEL-WIDE column at x=22 spanning y 0-105 - 100 px below 0.10, all in a single column, which is why an 'angular mass' was the wrong shape to look for. (2) it asked the idmask, got id 0 over the region, and stopped - while the MATMASK for the same frame sat beside it on disk and names the material in one query. The hanger-hook hypothesis it reached instead is refuted: no hanger is within 1500 mm of the frame's left margin, and the pixels are oak veneer. VERDICT keep: a shadow reveal between millwork and wall is a deliberate detail, the millwork run stands on the floor, and there is nothing to remove. NOT A CLAIM THAT WE FIXED IT: the feature is absent from p2r62 and p2r64 only because the eye camera MOVED after p2r55 (floor_poly_mm differs between the p2r54 and p2r58 dumps), so it is out of frame, not corrected. If the camera returns to p2r54's station the reveal returns with it, and it is legitimate when it does. The assembly key keeps its filed name so the history stays greppable (law 4: rows never leave the ledger). Filed p2r54, mis-probed p2r55, resolved from the matmask 2026-08-24.
